final_message:
The fix is complete. The issue was that the `get` method wasn't updating the recency of accessed keys. In an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache, when a key is accessed via `get()`, it should be marked as recently used by moving it to the end of the order list. Without this update, accessing key 1 didn't refresh its position, so when a new key was added, key 1 was incorrectly evicted instead of key 2 (which was actually older).

The fix adds two lines to the `get` method:
```python
self.order.remove(key)
self.order.append(key)
```

This moves the accessed key to the end of the order list, marking it as most recently used.
